title.narrative: Second Small and Microfinance Development Project

description.narrative: The Project facilitates access to credit by micro and small enterprises (MSEs) across Uzbekistan. It supports the generation of employment and sustains about 30,000 jobs for men and women. It contributes to inclusive economic growth. ADBs proposed intervention comprises (i) a loan of $50 million to be channeled through three participating commercial banks (PCBs) for onlending to viable MSEs; and (ii) a TA grant of $600,000 to improve PCBs MSE finance capacity and their subborrowers' entrepreneurial skills.

description.narrative: Expanded, viable and sustainable MSE finance operations

At the end of each year, and with respect to the total loan portfolio, PCBs have a delinquency and write-off ratio not exceeding 5% (Baseline: 2.5% in 2009) Progress/Status: On track for Ipak Yuli Bank and Hamkorbank. In regards to Agrobank, the following reservation is made. The AFS 2010 comes with a qualified opinion of the auditors. Part of this qualified opinion is due to AB's deviation from the international standards in financial reporting in connection with the misappropriation of funds in AB during February 2009 to February 2010. Essentially, the impact of the misappropriation of funds was not taken into account by AB in its financial statements for 2010. In particular, the funds that were misappropriated were not reflected as a loss, but as employee receivables. Data Source: PCBs' annual financial statements (audited) or other evidence provided to ADB by the PCBs Actual value:
